composing_text: 16th Infantry Regiment; 18th Infantry Regiment; 26th Infantry Regiment; 116th Infantry Regiment (29th Division)
notes: Assault division at Omaha (eastern half, Colleville sector). Beachhead only shallow at nightfall.

current_activity: advancing south toward Trévières and Mosles
notes: 18th Infantry drove south toward D-Day objectives north of Trevieres and the Mandeville-Mosles area; 26th Infantry released from reserve 17:45.

current_activity: taking part of Caumont (12 June claim)
notes: Wikipedia Operation Perch footnote: 1st US Infantry Division took part of Caumont on 12 June and the remainder the next day. Competing (earlier) claim. [Review (V-005): reference added. R343 (US Army Center of Military History, ETO order of battle, 1st Infantry Division, command and staff) lists Maj. Gen. Clarence R. Huebner as commanding general from 14 Dec 43 to 11 Dec 44. Nothing else changed.]

current_activity: holding Caumont on the V Corps left
notes: Caumont, on the left of the V Corps line, was held by the 1st Division by the end of 13 June (CMH). A Wikipedia footnote has the division taking part of the town on 12 June and the rest on 13 June (conflict G008).

CMH ETO-OB assignment table entry dated 15 July 1944. Location is the nearest listed CP at vicinity of Colombieres, Calvados (CMH ETO-OB), 1 days before the row date; the division position on the day is not stated. CMH gives the CP only as a vicinity of the town.

location_qualifier: objective of the 26 July attack; not the division position
current_activity: attacking toward Marigny with Combat Command B, 3rd Armored attached
notes: Event date: Breakout-13 p252: alerted on the afternoon of 25 July, General Huebner passed the 1st Division and attached CCB, 3rd Armored through the 9th Division on 26 July and attacked toward Marigny (CCB on the right of the road, the 18th Infantry on the left); the 353rd Division and 2nd SS Panzer Division elements stopped them short of the town that day. Event definition: division attack; Marigny is the objective, not the division position. Relationship: CCB, 3rd Armored attached for Cobra (text); corps and army entries from the CMH table. Batch 2 review: location_represents is objective, so the point is the named objective, not a documented position on the date (basis representative_point).

current_activity: division command post at Logis de la Bocage
notes: CMH ETO-OB lists the command post at vicinity of Logis de la Bocage, Manche on this date. CMH gives the CP only as a vicinity of the town. [Review (V-003): the CMH names the place but gives no site, and the earlier point (a house in Sartilly, about 21 km west of Brécey) was out of the division's sequence. The point is now a stand-in: Juvigny-le-Tertre (Wikipedia en), the place of the division command post listed on 3 August ("Juvigny (vic west)"), four days earlier. location_basis is nearest_earlier_command_post (location_date 1944-08-03), precision_km 10 -> 25 and confidence 0.5 -> 0.3 (rubric: a CP point 3 to 5 days away). The command post of 7 August itself is not located.] [Site search of 26 October 2026 (open item 6; point and precision unchanged): the name "Logis de la Bocage" was searched in the IGN geocoder (data.geopf.fr, place-name layer: no entry of that name; three hamlets named "le Logis" in Mortain-Bocage at about 48.608 N 0.910 W, 48.592 N 0.997 W and 48.582 N 0.956 W, and the Chateau du Logis at 48.591 N 0.997 W, none tied to the division by any source), OpenStreetMap Nominatim (only Le Vieux Logis, Sartilly, the earlier rejected point), the CMH 1st Infantry Division page (the same two entries, 4 and 7 August, "vic", Manche, no map reference) and the 90th Division after-action report of August 1944 (which has the 1st Division "moving east along the See River on Mortain"); the 1st Division after-action reports and G-3 journal (Eisenhower Library, accession 64-3) are not online. Breakout and Pursuit ch. 23 (pp. 443-445) has the division enter Mortain on the afternoon of 3 August and on 6 August displace south across the Selune to Gorron and Ambrieres-le-Grand. No source locates the site, so the stand-in is kept.]
